title: Give new_listener_coverage_test.dart a real seam into SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind instead of a hand-copied duplicate switch
rule: Feathers testability seam; Fowler duplication; TQ-8 (test-signal integrity)

evidence.quote:
/// Mirrors `SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind`. Public copy used by the
/// supervisor's onEvent handler in this test. If the production switch

why: The test file's own comment admits the risk: 'If the production switch changes, this duplicate will diverge.' Because SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind is private, the test cannot call the real one, so it wires its own copy into the ListenerSupervisor under test and then verifies that copy against itself. If a future change re-routes a channel to a different EntityKind in production (not just adds a new channel) without a matching edit here, this suite keeps passing against its own stale copy while production sync silently misroutes — the exact failure mode the file exists to prevent. This isn't hypothetical: lib/core/sync/tutored_listener_supervisor.dart already carries an independent third copy of the same switch, textually different from both (it omits 'learner_profiles' and 'tutor_grants'), showing this table has already drifted once in this codebase.
recommendation: Mark SyncOrchestratorImpl._channelToKind @visibleForTesting (or extract it to a small shared top-level function, e.g. core/sync/sync_channel_kind.dart, imported by both sync_orchestrator.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart) and have new_listener_coverage_test.dart import and call the real function instead of maintaining its own switch.
acceptance_criteria: new_listener_coverage_test.dart no longer defines its own _channelToKind; it imports and calls the production mapping function
adding a channel to FirestoreListenerSource without a matching production routing entry fails this suite (spot-checked by temporarily adding a mismatched channel)
